page: Microsoft Azure D16d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv4 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. The instance features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs, mapped from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual CPU. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 614 GB SSD, while it contains no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results position the D16d_v4 in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is measured at 1412.78, while multi-core performance reaches 14893.66. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block speed of 828.73 GB/sec and a large block read speed of 80.99 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the server achieves a static web serving throughput of 11.82 GB/sec and handles 13.99 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. For language model tasks, prompt processing with a small 135M model reaches 800.45 tokens per second, though performance drops to a weak rating of 24.49 tokens per second when processing prompts with a medium 7B model.

From a resource density perspective, the inclusion of a 614 GB local SSD alongside 64 GB of RAM provides a balanced hardware profile for workloads requiring temporary local storage without the overhead of external network-attached disks. The dedicated CPU allocation and average benchmark scores indicate stable performance for general-purpose workloads, database operations, static web serving, and software compilation.
